Q: Visual Studio 2026 cshtml pages intellisense not working A:

I had the same issue with VS2026. Removing these 2 lines from my project's .csproj file fixed the issue:

<RazorCompileOnBuild>false</RazorCompileOnBuild>

<RazorCompileOnPublish>false</RazorCompileOnPublish>

Q: Force S3 PDF to be viewed in browser instead of download A:

Check you file's metadata and remove Content-Disposition entry from that file. and set content type according to the file type.

Like for text file Content-Type='text/plain'

image png Content-Type='image/png'

pdf Content-Type=application/pdf

pdfxml Content-Type=application/vnd.adobe.pdfxml

If your file's Content-Type is binary/octet-stream then it will download instead of display.

Q: 2 scans instead of 1 in GROUP BY x HAVING EXISTS(..) A:

In that subquery, you can run as many filtered and unfiltered aggregates, repeated or original, and the planner won't care one bit as long as it can determine they're valid in the outer query.

I'm not sure how the code you referenced is relevant. That's a special optimisation for min() and/or max() calls that has nothing to do with the case at hand. It says so right on the tin:

/*-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * planagg.c
 *    Special planning for aggregate queries.
 *
 * This module tries to replace MIN/MAX aggregate functions by subqueries
 * of the form
 *      (SELECT col FROM tab
 *       WHERE col IS NOT NULL AND existing-quals
 *       ORDER BY col ASC/DESC
 *       LIMIT 1)
...
*/

The fragment you pointed at belongs to can_minmax_aggs

/*
 * can_minmax_aggs
 *      Examine all the aggregates in the query, and check if they are
 *      all MIN/MAX aggregates.  If so, build a list of MinMaxAggInfo
 *      nodes for them.
 *
 * Returns false if a non-MIN/MAX aggregate is found, true otherwise.
 */
static bool
can_minmax_aggs(PlannerInfo *root, List **context)

and it's meant to give up in case someone does only call min() but also adds some fancy filter() conditions that complicate the optimisation techniques that the whole thing tries to apply.

FILTER emulation with a CASE expression does not get you a simpler plan in PostgreSQL. If anything, it obfuscates your intention to the planner.

the planner misses the optimization of computing both aggregates in a single pass

That whole test case is there to make sure it can compute them in a single pass, because otherwise that syntax isn't supported. If it can't push it up and out, it doesn't spawn an additional aggregated subquery - it just throws an error.

Q: How to fix AssertJ Swing tests that are passing locally but failing in a CI server? A:

"Passes locally, fails in CI" with AssertJ-Swing almost always traces back to one of four root causes. Work through them in order — they're ranked by how often I've seen them bite real teams.

1. Headless / display mismatch. CI runners default to headless mode; Swing needs a real (or virtual) display. Check java.awt.headless — if it's true, AssertJ-Swing's robot can't pump events reliably. Provision a virtual display with Xvfb:

yaml
- run: |
    Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 &
    export DISPLAY=:99
    sleep 2
    mvn test

2. EDT timing differences. CI boxes are slower and noisier than your laptop, which exposes races between the Event Dispatch Thread and your assertions. AssertJ-Swing's default Robot delays are tuned for desktops. Bump them at suite start:

java
Robot robot = BasicRobot.robotWithNewAwtHierarchy();
robot.settings().delayBetweenEvents(50);     // default ~30ms
robot.settings().eventPostingDelay(100);     // default ~100ms
robot.settings().idleTimeout(10_000);

Also wrap every state read with GuiActionRunner.execute(...) — accessing Swing state off the EDT is the #1 source of intermittent failures that only show in CI.

3. Font / Look-and-Feel availability. If your tests query component sizes or use find by text, CI font metrics differ from your local JDK. Pin a font that ships with the JRE (Dialog, SansSerif) and set L&F explicitly in test setup rather than relying on the system default.

4. Window focus stealing. On shared CI agents, parallel jobs can steal focus mid-test. Run AssertJ-Swing tests serially (forkCount=1, reuseForks=true in Surefire) and prefer Frame.show() over setVisible(true) so AssertJ-Swing's focus monitor sees the window.

If you've ticked all four and still see intermittents, the failures are now genuinely flaky — meaning the same commit can pass or fail on identical inputs. At that point retrying masks the signal; you need to quarantine and quantify them before they erode trust in the suite.
